cli.name: help
cli.stdout:
Usage: harness <command> [arguments]

local AI project intelligence harness

Commands:
  version       Print version and build information
  init          Initialize harness state for this repository
  status        Show project, Git, database and client state
  sync          Refresh recorded project state (worktree, branch, HEAD)
  hooks         Install, uninstall or inspect optional hooks: Git sync and client tool events
  tasks         Operate the task queue (list, next, claim, complete, import...)
  proposals     Review memory proposals (list, show, approve, reject)
  memory        Show a memory's history, or retire one that no longer applies
  context       How often get_context contained what the work then changed (stats)
  projects      List the repositories on this machine that use harness, with their state
  workspace     Group this machine's projects into workspaces for cross-project search (list, create, join...)
  search        Search code in this project, or across its workspace (--workspace, --deep)
  metrics       How the MCP tools and provider capabilities fared: calls, errors, empty answers, latency
  report        Findings to steer harness: relevance, provider and tool health, bypasses, knowledge use
  ui            Open the local GUI: every harness project on this machine, its telemetry, knowledge and tasks
  doctor        Diagnose problems and suggest fixes
  docs          Read the documentation: the 'Using harness' guide and the reference, by section
  providers     Provider processes on this machine: graphify-csharp's warm C# sessions
  install       Add the harness MCP server to Claude Code / Codex config
  uninstall     Remove the harness MCP server from client config
  instructions  Add/update/remove the harness guidance: AGENTS.md (or an existing CLAUDE.md), one place only
  mcp           Serve MCP over stdio for host agents
  completion    Shell completion: print, install or remove it (zsh, bash, fish, PowerShell)
  telemetry     Opt-in export of aggregated usage reports to the harness developer (off by default)
  help          Show help (harness help <command> [<subcommand>])

Run 'harness <command> --help' (or 'harness help <command>') for a command's arguments and flags.

cli.name: task_help
cli.stdout:
Usage: harness tasks complete <id> [flags]

Complete a claimed task with evidence

Flags:
  -acc value
    	acceptance result "N=pass[:evidence]", "N=n/a:why" (repeat for each criterion)
  -acc-all string
    	report every criterion at once, e.g. "pass:see tests"
  -check value
    	validation "command=pass" (repeatable)
  -commit string
    	commit id
  -json
    	machine-readable output
  -project string
    	directory inside the repository (default ".")
  -summary string
    	what changed (required)

tools.description: The architecture findings of this project (scope project, default) or between the services of its workspaces (scope workspace), read from the files now: kind, level, basis (fact, or heuristic: read from names or thresholds), title, why, what could help, evidence (file:line), status since the last change (new, changed, unchanged, gone) and the author's mark (by design with the reason, back for review, or a task); a boundary finding names the recorded rule it breaks. Boundary rules are knowledge: lines such as 'group Domain = *.Domain', 'layers: Api > BL > DAL', 'forbid: Domain -> *.DAL', 'only: Application -> Domain' in a constraint, decision or convention (propose new ones with memory_propose). Drift (a broken rule, or knowledge naming code that is gone: stale-knowledge) can be resolved either way: propose a corrected statement with memory_propose (supersedes = the rule's memory) or a task fixing the code with architecture_propose. Without a filter the answer is a summary by kind and one line per finding; filter by kind or area (a path prefix; for workspace findings also a member's name), or give a key, for findings in full (why, what could help, every place). Explain and suggest; never act on a finding until it is a task. Architectural tasks and by-design marks are the author's: propose them to the user, never create them. A finding marked by design is intended (its reason says why): do not raise it again; one back for review grew since it was marked.

scope.description: project (default) or workspace: the system findings between the services of this project's workspaces

key.description: one finding in full, by its key

full.description: every finding in full (by default, without a kind, area or key filter, a summary and one short line each)

area.description: only findings about this path prefix (the unit or any evidence); for workspace findings also a member's name

kind.description: only this kind, e.g. cycle, layering, unused, deep-import, chatty, contract-unserved, shared-database

hide_marked.description: leave out findings the author marked by design (by default they are listed with the reason)

gone.description: also list findings gone since the last change (a task's shows it resolved)

snippets.description: also the code at each listed finding's evidence (the function it names, a repeated run, lines around a line), within a size budget: to judge whether a finding is real

tools.name: architecture_findings

tools.description: Propose an architectural task or a by-design mark for the user to approve; nothing changes until they do (harness ui, Work › Inbox), so tell them. kind 'task': from a finding (finding = its key from architecture_findings) or from your own observation (no finding; title, reason = what should change and why, evidence = the places that show it; it is recorded as your interpretation, apart from harness's findings). kind 'by_design': a finding (key) and reason = why it is intended. scope workspace for a finding between services. Never add architectural tasks to a backlog file or create them yourself: this rule is steered by the tools and instructions, not enforced. Other tasks keep the usual flow.

finding.description: the finding's key (from architecture_findings); required for by_design, empty for a task from your own observation

scope.description: project (default) or workspace: a finding between the services of this project's workspaces

reason.description: task: what should change and why; by_design: why it is intended

evidence.description: own observation: the places that show it (path:line)

tools.name: architecture_propose

tools.description: Files that change together, from the Git history. file: its partners (commits shared, share of its commits; from providers offering arch.change_coupling). check: the usual partners (3+ shared commits, half or more of the commits of a file with 5+) of the changed files that the change leaves out — run it before you finish a change; files: the change (default: the uncommitted changes). Neither: the hotspots, the code files that changed most in the last 180 days, with their usual partners. A reminder of what usually changes too, never a rule: decide from the code whether it needs changing.

file.description: a file (path from the project root): its co-change partners

check.description: check a change for usual partners it leaves out

files.description: with check: the changed files (default: the uncommitted changes)

tools.name: change_coupling

tools.description: Get the context for a task in one call, within a size budget: the relevant code grouped by file, with the areas (top-level directories) it spans (definitions with bodies while they fit, otherwise drill-down references; callers and impact), the decisions, conventions, constraints and warnings that apply to it, the architecture findings touching that code (as of the last sync, with the author's marks: explain and suggest, never act on one until it is a task), and recent changes. Describe the task in words and name the symbols you know. Read or search further only for what is still missing.

library.description: the library's member name in the workspace (as search results name projects)

type.description: one of: goal, constraint, decision, fact, open_question, warning, convention
